Title: Efficiently Testing Laravel Code Changes Without Refreshing the Page Every Time

Body:

In this comprehensive blog post, we will address one of the most common pain points for Laravel developers: running code changes in a Laravel project without refreshing the page. Using efficient techniques and best practices, we can considerably improve our development workflow and save time by eliminating the need for constant refreshes.

To achieve this, we will focus on two crucial aspects of working with Laravel projects: setting up an ideal development environment and taking advantage of useful tools such as live server and browser refresh triggers. Let's explore both:

1. Setting Up a Development Environment

An efficient Laravel project development environment ensures a seamless integration between the code editor, terminal, and web browser. Some essential steps to set up your ideal environment are:

   a. Installation of Composer: If you haven't already, install Composer globally on your system to manage project dependencies. This will ensure that all libraries and necessary files are installed automatically upon running the command "composer update" or "composer install".
   
   b. Laravel Project Setup: Create a new application using the "laravel new appname" command, where 'appname' is your desired project name. This command will initialize and configure a fresh Laravel installation for you.
   
   c. Installing PHP, Apache and MySQL (LAMP) or Composer on your local machine: If you haven't already, it's essential to have a solid development stack installed. Ensure that the versions of these applications are compatible with the current Laravel version.
   
   d. Set Up Environment Variables and Database Configuration: Use a .env file in your project root folder for storing database credentials and other sensitive information. This will allow you to securely manage your application configuration.
   
   2. Using Live Server and Browser Refresh Triggers

Once you've set up an optimal development environment, the following techniques can help streamline your Laravel workflow by automating the code refreshing process:

   a. Enable PHP Artisan Serve: The "php artisan serve" command runs the development server on localhost and automatically refreshes changes when detected. However, it's advised to use a different live server for smoother performance with more advanced features. Some popular options include Laravel Valet or Local by Flywheel (for Mac), and XAMPP or WampServer (for Windows).
   
   b. Integrate Live Server with a Code Editor: Utilize an IDE, such as PHPStorm, that supports live server integration. This will allow you to view changes directly in the browser without refreshing. Alternatively, you can use extensions like LiveReload for VSCode or LiveServer for Sublime Text to achieve the same results.
   
   c. Use Browser Cache Busting Techniques: When working with a team or collaborating on an application, consider using tools such as Laravel Mix and Webpack to bundle assets and keep track of file versions. This ensures that changes are instantly reflected in your application without manual refreshes.
   
   d. Explore LiveView or VueJS for Real-Time Updates: LiveView is a new feature introduced in Laravel 6 that allows you to create real-time applications with minimal effort. It automatically updates the UI when server-side changes occur, eliminating the need to refresh manually. Additionally, using JavaScript frameworks like VueJS can provide similar functionality via live data binding and event handling.

In conclusion, setting up an efficient development environment and leveraging appropriate tools can significantly improve your Laravel experience by minimizing the need for refreshing pages after code changes. By implementing a combination of these techniques, you will ensure a smooth workflow that ultimately saves time and frustration during development. Remember to keep your development setup updated and optimized for maximum efficiency.
